supports http with nodejs should parse t: real gap, now classified (plan.md phase 2: "fix: parse a numeric-string timeout like axios"): axios accepts a numeric string (`timeout: '250'`) via `parseInt(timeout, 10)`; this library only parses `timeout` for its own deadline-timer logic and passes the original string through to undici's `headersTimeout`/`bodyTimeout` unparsed, which undici rejects (`ERR_BAD_REQUEST`, "invalid headersTimeout") instead of enforcing the parsed value and giving `ECONNABORTED`/"timeout of 250ms exceeded" like axios. Confirmed with a direct repro against the built package.
supports http with nodejs should support: real gap, now classified (plan.md phase 2: "fix: wrap a throwing beforeRedirect like axios"): a `beforeRedirect` callback that throws propagates the raw, unwrapped `Error` here (`code: undefined`, `name: 'Error'`); axios (`follow-redirects`) wraps it as "Redirected request failed: <message>". Confirmed with a direct repro against the built package.

supports http with nodejs should wrap HT: plan.md phase 2 "fix: remaining error-shape gaps", item 3 ("HTTP and interceptor errors should keep the call-site stack, as axios does") - decided not to implement: a literal port of axios' mechanism (Axios.prototype.request's catch block re-capturing and appending a fresh Error.captureStackTrace) measured 40%+ CPU/req on an all-error workload even capped at stackTraceLimit: 1, for materially less benefit than in axios, since this package's request path is an RxJS Observable - confirmed directly (with both a minimal repro and this package's own axiosRef pipeline) that neither a real HTTP error nor a synchronously-thrown interceptor error keeps a link back to the caller of axiosRef.get()/firstValueFrom() the way axios' own await/.then() chain does. This test asserts the stack contains exactly one occurrence of the caller's own function name, which this package's stack does not.

Separately, `formDataHeaderPolicy` itself isn't implemented either way (documented: docs/axios-supported-options.md#progress-callbacks-maxrate-and-formserializer).

supports http with nodejs request aborti: real gap, newly classified (plan.md phase 2: "fix: abort a responseType: 'stream' response when the caller's AbortSignal fires after emission"): once the stream has been handed back, calling `.abort()` on the caller's own `AbortSignal` no longer has any effect - the stream keeps flowing indefinitely instead of being destroyed with `ERR_CANCELED`, as axios does. This is a different code path from the already-documented RxJS-unsubscribe-after-emission difference (see docs/axios-supported-options.md#httpservice): this is the caller's own signal, not an Observable unsubscribe. Confirmed with a direct repro against the built package (the stream never closed).

supports http with nodejs Rate limit sho: plan.md phase 2: slow response-body consumption fails with UND_ERR_SOCKET "other side closed" against a Node server whose keepAliveTimeout is short (1s here; the 5s default too).
